notes: Every eval's output must also pass scripts/check_output.py (structure, ratings, citations, verdict consistency, dated sources, no placeholders). The expectations below cover what the script can't judge on its own; grade them with agents/grader.md from skill-creator.

evals.name: multi-segment-company
evals.prompt: Let's do a Five Forces analysis on Swiggy
evals.expected_output: An analysis of Swiggy's main profit-driving segment (India food delivery) with Instamart noted separately, saved as Competitive Strategy/swiggy-food-delivery-five-forces.md.
expectations: The output file passes scripts/check_output.py with every check passing
The industry boundary names one segment (food delivery) and says what is excluded
Instamart / quick commerce is mentioned but not mixed into the five ratings
The filename includes the segment (swiggy-food-delivery-five-forces.md)
Reference peers are named and the file has no full Peer comparison section, since the user didn't ask for one
Zomato/Eternal figures are used to judge Swiggy's position (larger or smaller, higher or lower margin)
The margin check uses at least 3 periods of segment margin data, with sources
The final chat reply gives the file path, the three summary lines and at most two gaps, and doesn't repeat the full analysis

evals.name: explicit-peer-comparison
evals.prompt: can you compare zerodha vs groww vs upstox on competitive positioning? which one actually has the better moat in indian retail broking
evals.expected_output: A five-forces file for the first-named company (Zerodha) that includes a Peer comparison section with a forces × companies table, separating 'most favorable structure' from 'strongest execution'.
expectations: The output file passes scripts/check_output.py with every check passing
The file is named zerodha-five-forces.md (focal company first) and saved in Competitive Strategy/
There is a Peer comparison section with a table: the five forces as rows, Zerodha, Groww and Upstox as columns
The peer section answers both questions separately: which company has the most favorable structure, and which has the strongest execution
Active-client or market-share figures are cited with a source and date, or marked 'not disclosed' with the proxy named
Regulatory changes (e.g. SEBI F&O rules, true-to-label fees) appear as evidence with dates

evals.name: segment-and-punctuation-naming
evals.prompt: How durable is AT&T's competitive position in US wireless? I keep hearing it's a commoditized three-player market
evals.expected_output: A wireless-segment analysis saved as Competitive Strategy/att-wireless-five-forces.md (punctuation dropped, segment appended), addressing the user's 'commoditized' framing with evidence.
expectations: The output file passes scripts/check_output.py with every check passing
The filename drops the ampersand and adds the segment, e.g. att-wireless-five-forces.md
The boundary is US wireless and excludes AT&T's fiber/broadband business, or treats it as a substitute
The analysis tests the 'commoditized' claim directly (e.g. churn, ARPU trend, promotions) rather than assuming it
Cable MVNOs (Comcast/Charter) are covered under new entrants or rivalry, with evidence
The positioning section ties AT&T's wireless margins over the last 3–5 years to its rating

evals.name: existing-file-not-overwritten
evals.prompt: Run five forces on Swiggy again, I want a fresh take
evals.expected_output: Because Competitive Strategy/swiggy-food-delivery-five-forces.md already exists, the new analysis is saved under a date-suffixed name and the original file is left unchanged.
expectations: The output file passes scripts/check_output.py with every check passing
The new file is saved as swiggy-food-delivery-five-forces-YYYY-MM-DD.md (today's date)
The existing swiggy-food-delivery-five-forces.md is unchanged
The chat reply says a previous analysis existed and gives the new file's path

evals.name: thin-evidence-private-company
evals.prompt: Do a porter's five forces on Zepto — I know they're private so data may be patchy
evals.expected_output: An analysis that sets confidence to low wherever evidence is thin, uses 'not disclosed' plus a named proxy instead of invented numbers, and lists the missing data under Gaps.
expectations: The output file passes scripts/check_output.py with every check passing
At least one force is rated low or medium confidence, with the reason stated
Any figure that isn't public (e.g. margins, order volumes) is marked 'not disclosed' or credited to a named secondary source (DRHP, Redseer, press)
No precise number appears without a source
Gaps lists at least 2 specific items, each saying what would be needed to verify it
